paragraphs: In the morning, receive a design change and revise the 3D model. Produce part drawings, specify tolerances, and write processes. At midday, inspect a sample on the shop floor for manufacturability. In the afternoon, update BOMs and versions, release drawings, archive them, and answer process questions.

In short, they turn parts into manufacturable drawings. They draw parts, specify tolerances and materials, create assembly and process drawings, check standards, and coordinate the shop floor until machines can build from the drawings.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 42,900 Mechanical Drafters were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to fall to 40,100 by 2034, a net loss of about 2,800 jobs, with around 3,300 openings annually and a 2026 median annual wage of about $68,500 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace knowledgeable Mechanical Drafters, but it will reduce junior roles. Parametric and 3D tools automate repetitive drawing, shifting drafters from drawing toward tolerance expertise, process planning, and quality control. Tracing-only roles face pressure, while professionals who understand processes and prevent errors gain value.
